To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

a panel of monoclanal and polyclanal antibodies was generated, that together they were able to recognize ORF1a encoded PRRSV ns1-ns8, and using these reagents, we were able to detect replicase cleavage intermediates in virus infected cells.

we generated and characterized a panel of monoclanal and polyclonals that recognize all PRRSV nonstructural proteins (nsPs) encoded by the ORF1a, and used this reagent to identify the localization and cleavage products of PRRSV non-structural proteins.

we have identified and characterized a panel of antibodies that recognize eight PRRSV nsPs, and that we have shown that the majority of these nsps co-localize in the perinucleus of PRRSV-infecetd cells.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification and subcellu- lar localization of PRRS virus (PRRS virus) non-structural proteins.
the identification and characterization of the PRRSV ns proteins and their role in viral replication.
the identification and localization of the non-structural proteins of PRRSV.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the PRRSV antibody set described in this study is a valuable tool that will be of great use to the research community for further studies on the replication, structure and function of PRRSV.
the PRRSV replicase polyprotein (pp1a) is processed by two viral proteinases, one cleaving at the nsp1/2 and nsp7/8 boundaries and a second at the nsp2/3, nsp3/4, nsp4/5 and nsp5/6 junctions.
we have identified eight ORF1-encoded non-structural viral proteins in PRRSV infected MARC-145 and PK-15 cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have identified a panel of monoclals and polyclonals that can be used to identify PRRS virus nsps in virus infected cells and tissues.
we have identified eight PRRSV nsproteins and have shown that they localize in the perinucleus of infected cells.
we have generated a panel of monocloal and polyclonl antibodies against the PRRSV ORF1a proteins, and we have shown that these proteins can be detected in virus-infected MARC 145 cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that

we have developed a panel of monoclanal and polyclanl antibodies that recognize the non-structural proteins of PRRSV, and that we have been able to use these antibodies to detect the non-structural proteins of PRRSV in infected cells.
we have identified a panel of antibodies against the PRRSV ns proteins.
the PRRSV ORF1a replicase is processed into ten nsps, and that the nsp1, nsp7 and nsp8 regions are cleaved internally, yielding the nsps nsp1α/β, nsp7/β and nsp1/8, respectively.
